The bill’s proposed “Mold Awareness and Registration Act” would require the executive director of the Department of Public Health and Environment to issue a registration to a person who provides mold remediation or assessment services in Colorado if the person applies for registration and provides evidence of an active third-party remediation or assessment certification and evidence of financial responsibility. |

## EPA residential mold-remediation guidance

| Topic | Direct wording and figures |
|---|---|
| Small mold area | “If the moldy area is less than about 10 square feet (less than roughly a 3 ft. by 3 ft. patch), in most cases, you can handle the job yourself, follow the Mold Cleanup Tips and Techniques.” |
| Extensive mold or water damage | “If there has been a lot of water damage, and/or mold growth covers more than 10 square feet, consult EPA guide Mold Remediation in Schools and Commercial Buildings.” |
| Applicability of EPA guide | “Although focused on schools and commercial buildings, this document is applicable to other building types.” |
| Hiring a contractor | “If you choose to hire a contractor (or other professional service provider) to do the cleanup, make sure the contractor has experience cleaning up mold.” |
| Contractor guidance | “Check references and ask the contractor to follow the recommendations in EPA guide Mold Remediation in Schools and Commercial Buildings, the guidelines of the American Conference of Governmental Industrial Hygienists (ACGIH); Institute of Inspection, Cleaning and Restoration Certification (IICRC); or other guidelines from professional or government organizations.” |
| HVAC contamination | “If you suspect that the heating/ventilation/air conditioning (HVAC) system may be contaminated with mold (it is part of an identified moisture problem, for instance, or there is mold near the intake to the system), consult EPA guide Should You Have the Air Ducts in Your Home Cleaned? before taking further action.” |
| Contaminated HVAC operation | “Do not run the HVAC system if you know or suspect that it is contaminated with mold - it could spread mold throughout the building.” |
| Sewage or contaminated water | “If the water and/or mold damage was caused by sewage or other contaminated water, then call in a professional who has experience cleaning and fixing buildings damaged by contaminated water.” |
| Health concerns | “If you have health concerns, consult a health professional before starting cleanup.” |
| Hard surfaces | “Scrub mold off hard surfaces with detergent and water, and dry completely.” |
| Porous materials | “Absorbent or porous materials, such as ceiling tiles and carpet, may have to be thrown away if they become moldy.” |
| Painting or caulking | “Do not paint or caulk moldy surfaces. Clean up the mold and dry the surfaces before painting.” |
